svg.title: The $550,000 Base-Case Profit Bridge
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-owner-profit-bridge; chart type: waterfall; title: The $550,000 Base-Case Profit Bridge; subtitle: Six bars reconcile recognized revenue to $165,000 annual owner net profit.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Annual USD. First and last bars are totals; the four middle bars are signed deductions. The $550,000 revenue, 30.0% margin, and $165,000 owner net profit are canonical. Expense categories are an illustrative allocation of the required $385,000 total costs, not additional scorecard facts.; caption: $550,000 - $210,000 - $65,000 - $42,000 - $68,000 = $165,000; $165,000 / $550,000 = 30.0%. Do not add the closing profit total as another cash inflow.; stages: label: Recognized agency revenue; value: $550,000 from accepted implementations and earned retainers; numeric value: 550000.0; detail: Illustrative mix: 22 implementations at $15,000 produce $330,000; 110 earned client-months of support at $2,000 produce $220,000. Neither client revenue nor projected automation savings enters this total.; label: Delivery labor; value: Subtract $210,000 for employee and contractor delivery; numeric value: -210000.0; detail: Allocate delivery compensation and associated labor burdens across the two full-time and three contractor seats. Contractor engagements are fractional; this budget is not five full-time salaries. Balance: $340,000.; label: Client workload costs; value: Subtract $65,000 for attributable runtime and service usage; numeric value: -65000.0; detail: Assign model usage, retrieval infrastructure, and workflow execution costs to client projects. These variable delivery costs sit outside recurring overhead in this illustrative bridge. Balance: $275,000.; label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $42,000 for shared tools and business operations; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget $3,500 monthly for shared software, insurance, accounting, and routine administration. This lies within the $2,500–$18,000 monthly operating range; that range is not the all-in annual cost ceiling. Balance: $233,000.; label: Other recognized costs; value: Subtract $68,000 for acquisition, rework, and remaining expenses; numeric value: -68000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $30,000 to acquisition, $20,000 to delivery remediation, and $18,000 to remaining recognized expenses. Keep these separate from labor and shared overhead; replace allocations with actual ledger categories. Balance: $165,000.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $165,000 residual profit at exactly 30.0% margin; numeric value: 165000.0; detail: Closing total after all four expense deductions, not gross margin or owner take-home after personal taxes. No client transaction volume or unrealized efficiency benefit contributes to this residual.

circle.title: label: Recognized agency revenue; value: $550,000 from accepted implementations and earned retainers; numeric value: 550000.0; detail: Illustrative mix: 22 implementations at $15,000 produce $330,000; 110 earned client-months of support at $2,000 produce $220,000. Neither client revenue nor projected automation savings enters this total.

label: Delivery labor; value: Subtract $210,000 for employee and contractor delivery; numeric value: -210000.0; detail: Allocate delivery compensation and associated labor burdens across the two full-time and three contractor seats. Contractor engagements are fractional; this budget is not five full-time salaries. Balance: $340,000.

label: Client workload costs; value: Subtract $65,000 for attributable runtime and service usage; numeric value: -65000.0; detail: Assign model usage, retrieval infrastructure, and workflow execution costs to client projects. These variable delivery costs sit outside recurring overhead in this illustrative bridge. Balance: $275,000.

label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $42,000 for shared tools and business operations; numeric value: -42000.0; detail: Budget $3,500 monthly for shared software, insurance, accounting, and routine administration. This lies within the $2,500–$18,000 monthly operating range; that range is not the all-in annual cost ceiling. Balance: $233,000.

label: Other recognized costs; value: Subtract $68,000 for acquisition, rework, and remaining expenses; numeric value: -68000.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $30,000 to acquisition, $20,000 to delivery remediation, and $18,000 to remaining recognized expenses. Keep these separate from labor and shared overhead; replace allocations with actual ledger categories. Balance: $165,000.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $165,000 residual profit at exactly 30.0% margin; numeric value: 165000.0; detail: Closing total after all four expense deductions, not gross margin or owner take-home after personal taxes. No client transaction volume or unrealized efficiency benefit contributes to this residual.

text.title: Assumptions: Annual USD. First and last bars are totals; the four middle bars are signed deductions. The $550,000 revenue, 30.0% margin, and $165,000 owner net profit are canonical. Expense categories are an illustrative allocation of the required $385,000 total costs, not additional scorecard facts.
